deterministic_checks.method: Independent plain-JavaScript direct-DFT implementation; no component helper was imported.
results: PASS: single N=64,Q=1 gives f_hat=176 Hz, original spacing 16 Hz, e_bin=0.1875, FAIL target.
PASS: single N=64,Q=2 gives f_hat=176 Hz, e_bin=0.1875, FAIL target.
PASS: single N=64,Q=4 gives f_hat=172 Hz, e_bin=0.0625, PASS and the first allowed Q pass.
PASS: single N=64,Q=16 gives f_hat=173 Hz and e_bin=0 exactly.
PASS: pair N=64,Q=16 gives phase-0 candidates [171] Hz and phase-90 candidates [166,187] Hz; the two-phase rule fails.
PASS: pair N=128,Q=16 gives phase-0 candidates [159,169.5,180.5,190.5] Hz and phase-90 candidate [171] Hz; the two-phase rule fails.

PASS: pair N=256,Q=4 gives phase-0 candidates [164,170,175,180] Hz and phase-90 candidates [164,170,180] Hz; both contain the required 170/180 Hz peaks with a lower intervening sample, so the rule passes.
PASS: the short and long pair controls both have L=1024 and 1 Hz displayed spacing; apertures are 62.5/250 ms and main-lobe widths are 32/8 Hz.
PASS: all 80 combinations of four N values, five Q values, two modes, and phase endpoints 0/90 produce nonempty finite spectra and finite SVG coordinates.

pedagogy.D1: PASS: changing padding and acquired duration exposes interpolation versus phase-stable resolution while holding the relevant control fixed.
pedagogy.D2: PASS: fixed-band direct sums and all derived state update synchronously; there are no effects, async calls, network calls, or transitions.
pedagogy.D3_alive_on_arrival: PASS: the initial Padded pair state is N=64,Q=16,L=1024,phi=0 and visibly reports one 171 Hz peak plus a two-phase FAIL on a dense 1 Hz grid.
pedagogy.D3_presets: PASS: Coarse tone, Padded tone, Padded pair, and Long pair exactly match the prose/preflight; Phase 0 degrees and Phase 90 degrees are native-button anchors.
pedagogy.D4: PASS: Coarse tone to Q=4 reaches the strict interpolation PASS, Padded pair shows the required failure, and Long pair reaches the two-phase PASS at the same L and grid.
pedagogy.D5: FAIL only on 360px in-chart text legibility; the component otherwise passes the one-file, 134-LOC, client-boundary, dependency, keyboard, touch, and responsive-width requirements.

accessibility_and_visual.controls: PASS: all controls are UI-kit native buttons/ranges; the rendered minimum control height is 44 CSS px; sliders have explicit labels and aria-valuetext.
accessibility_and_visual.announcements: PASS: TargetList and Readout provide polite live status; the SVG has a state-specific accessible name.
accessibility_and_visual.keyboard: PASS by native-control/source audit: presets are buttons and every parameter is an input type=range; active preset clearing follows all four stored values.
accessibility_and_visual.non_color: PASS: truth frequencies are directly labelled, the alternate phase is dashed, and PASS/FAIL plus numeric peak lists do not depend on hue.
accessibility_and_visual.themes: PASS apart from the shared mobile text-size defect: static initial rendering used the real compiled CSS in light and dark; colors resolve to theme tokens/currentColor, with no fixed light background or horizontal overflow.
accessibility_and_visual.mobile_360: FAIL: the actual lesson leaves 312 px after page padding and 278 px inside the Panel. The 360-unit SVG therefore scales by 0.772; its 10-unit peak/tick/axis labels render at about 7.72 CSS px and its 12-unit title at about 9.27 CSS px. No clipping or horizontal overflow was found, but the chart text is not readable at the required phone width.

required_fixes.issue: At the required 360px viewport, the responsive 360-unit SVG shrinks its 10-12 unit labels to about 7.72-9.27 CSS px. The chart fits and both themes are otherwise sound, but its peak, tick, title, and axis text are too small for the demo checklist's readable-phone requirement.
required_fixes.required: Use a mobile-specific SVG layout or responsive text treatment that keeps every in-chart label legible at 360px without clipping, horizontal scrolling, or removing the direct labels/non-color cues.
